general.q: What is at the centre of our solar system?
general.e: The Sun is a star, and everything else orbits around it.

general.q: How many planets are in our solar system?
general.e: There are eight planets, from Mercury to Neptune.

general.q: What force keeps the planets orbiting the Sun?
general.e: The Sun's gravity pulls the planets so they curve around it instead of flying off.

general.q: Where is the asteroid belt?
general.e: Millions of rocky asteroids orbit between Mars and Jupiter.

general.q: What is the name of our galaxy?
general.e: Our solar system is in the Milky Way galaxy.

general.q: Why can't you hear sounds in space?
a: There is no air to carry sound
general.e: Sound needs air (or another material) to travel through, and space is nearly empty.

general.q: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
general.e: Neil Armstrong stepped onto the Moon in 1969.

general.q: About how long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
general.e: Light travels fast, but the Sun is far away: roughly 8 minutes.

general.q: What is a shooting star really?
a: A tiny space rock burning up in our atmosphere
general.e: It is a meteor: a small bit of rock or dust glowing as it burns up high above Earth.

general.q: What was the name of the first artificial satellite, launched in 1957?
general.e: The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1 and started the space age.

general.q: What do we call a pattern of stars, like Orion or the Big Dipper?
general.e: People have drawn pictures in the stars, called constellations, for thousands of years.

general.q: What is a black hole?
a: A place where gravity is so strong not even light escapes
general.e: A black hole's gravity is so strong that nothing, not even light, can get out.

general.q: What does the Moon's gravity cause on Earth's oceans?
general.e: The Moon's pull makes the ocean rise and fall twice a day: the tides.

general.q: What is the International Space Station?
a: A science lab where astronauts live, orbiting Earth
A giant telescope on the Moon
general.e: The ISS circles Earth about every 90 minutes with astronauts on board.

general.q: A comet is mostly made of…
general.e: Comets are dirty snowballs. Their glowing tails form when the Sun heats the ice.

general.q: What is the name of the NASA rover that landed on Mars in 2021 with the Ingenuity helicopter?
general.e: Perseverance landed in 2021, and Ingenuity became the first helicopter to fly on another planet.

general.q: What is the Sun mostly made of?
general.e: The Sun is a ball of hot hydrogen and helium gas. Hydrogen fuses into helium to make its light.

general.q: What causes day and night on Earth?
a: Earth moving closer and farther from the Sun
general.e: Earth turns once about every 24 hours, so each side faces the Sun, then faces away.

general.q: What do we call the path a planet takes around the Sun?
general.e: Every planet follows a curved path called an orbit.

general.q: How many moons does Earth have?
general.e: Earth has one natural moon, which we simply call the Moon.

general.q: What is a light-year?
a: The distance light travels in one year
A year on a bright planet
The time it takes the Sun to rise
general.e: Light zooms about 9.5 trillion kilometres in a year. A light-year measures distance, not time.

general.q: Which space telescope, launched in 1990, has been taking pictures of the universe for decades?
general.e: The Hubble Space Telescope orbits Earth and has sent back thousands of amazing images.

general.q: The James Webb Space Telescope is mainly built to see which kind of light?
general.e: Infrared lets Webb peer through dust clouds and see the faint light from the first galaxies.

general.q: Why do astronauts seem to float inside the space station?
a: They are falling around Earth together with the station
There is no gravity at all up there
general.e: Gravity is still strong there. Astronauts and the station are in constant free fall around Earth, so they feel weightless.

general.q: What is the layer of gases around a planet called?
general.e: The atmosphere is the blanket of gases around a planet. Earth's has the oxygen we breathe.

general.q: What is a satellite?
a: An object that orbits a bigger object in space
general.e: The Moon is a natural satellite of Earth. Spacecraft that circle Earth are artificial satellites.

general.q: What do we call a piece of space rock that survives the fall and lands on the ground?
general.e: In space it is a meteoroid, in the sky it is a meteor, and on the ground it is a meteorite.

general.q: About how old is our solar system?
general.e: The Sun and planets formed together around 4.6 billion years ago.

general.q: In which direction does the Sun rise?
general.e: Earth spins toward the east, so the Sun appears to come up in the east.

Mercury.q: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
Mercury.e: Mercury orbits closest to the Sun.

Mercury.q: A year on Mercury (one trip around the Sun) lasts about…
Mercury.e: Mercury is so close to the Sun that it zooms around in just 88 Earth days.

Mercury.q: How big is Mercury compared with the other planets?
a: It is the same size as Earth
Mercury.e: Mercury is the smallest planet, only a little bigger than our Moon.

Venus.q: Which planet is the hottest, thanks to thick clouds that trap heat?
Venus.e: Venus's thick atmosphere traps heat, making it hotter even than Mercury.

Venus.q: Venus spins in a direction that is…
a: Side to side like a coin
Venus.e: Venus rotates backwards (retrograde), so the Sun rises in the west there.

Venus.q: Venus shines so brightly at dawn and dusk that people call it…
a: The Morning Star or Evening Star
Venus.e: Venus is not really a star. It is a planet reflecting lots of sunlight.

Earth.q: About how much of Earth's surface is covered by water?
Earth.e: Around 71% of Earth is water, which is why it looks blue from space.

Earth.q: Which gas do plants make that we need to breathe?
About how long does Earth take to go once around the Sun?
Earth.e: One trip around the Sun is a year, and that is why a year has about 365 days.

Mars.q: Why is Mars called the Red Planet?
a: It is covered in red oceans
Mars.e: Iron in the soil has rusted, giving Mars its red colour.

Mars.q: What is the name of the giant volcano on Mars, the tallest in the solar system?
Mars.e: Olympus Mons is about 2.5 times taller than Mount Everest.

Mars.q: What are the names of Mars's two moons?
Mars.e: Phobos and Deimos are small, lumpy moons.

Mars.q: Which robot rovers have explored Mars?
Mars.e: Curiosity and Perseverance are car-sized rovers that drive around Mars studying rocks.

Jupiter.q: Which is the largest planet in our solar system?
Jupiter.e: Jupiter is bigger than all the other planets put together.

Jupiter.q: The Great Red Spot on Jupiter is a giant…
Jupiter.e: It is a huge storm, wider than Earth.

Jupiter.q: Jupiter is mostly made of which gases?
Jupiter.e: Jupiter is a gas giant with no solid surface to stand on.

Saturn.q: Saturn's rings are mostly made of…
Saturn.e: The rings are billions of chunks of ice, from dust-sized to house-sized.

Saturn.q: Which planet is so light for its size that it could float in water?
Saturn.e: Saturn is mostly hydrogen and helium, so it is less dense than water.

Saturn.q: Which spacecraft orbited Saturn for 13 years, ending in 2017?
Saturn.e: Cassini studied Saturn, its rings and its moons before diving into the planet in 2017.

Uranus.q: What is unusual about the way Uranus spins?
a: It is tilted on its side
It spins faster than any planet
Uranus.e: Uranus is tipped over so far that it rolls around the Sun on its side.

Uranus.q: Which gas gives Uranus its blue-green colour?
Uranus.e: Methane absorbs red light, leaving the blue-green glow.
Herschel spotted it through his telescope, and it was the first planet found with one.

Neptune.q: Which planet is farthest from the Sun?
Neptune.e: Neptune is the eighth and farthest planet.

Neptune.q: Which planet has the fastest winds in the solar system?
Neptune.e: Neptune's winds can reach over 1,000 miles per hour.

Neptune.q: About how long does Neptune take to orbit the Sun once?
Neptune.e: Neptune is so far away that it has only gone around the Sun once since its discovery in 1846.

Moon.q: About how long does the Moon take to orbit Earth?
Moon.e: The Moon circles Earth roughly every 27 to 29 days. That is where the word "month" comes from.

Moon.q: The large dark plains you can see on the Moon are called…
Moon.e: Early astronomers thought they were seas. They are really ancient plains of cooled lava.

Moon.q: How strong is the Moon's gravity compared with Earth's?
Moon.e: On the Moon you would weigh only about one sixth of what you weigh on Earth.

Moon.q: Which mission first landed humans on the Moon?
Moon.e: Apollo 11 landed Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin on the Moon in 1969.

Ceres.q: Ceres is a dwarf planet found in…
a: The far edge of the solar system
Ceres.e: Ceres lives in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter.

Ceres.q: What did the Dawn spacecraft find shining on Ceres?
Ceres.e: The bright spots in Occator crater are deposits of salts left behind when salty water froze and dried.

Europa.q: Europa is a moon of which planet?
Europa.e: Europa is one of Jupiter's four biggest moons.

Europa.q: What may be hiding under Europa's icy shell?
Europa.e: Scientists think Europa holds more liquid water than all of Earth's oceans combined.

Europa.q: Which NASA spacecraft is on its way to study Europa?
Europa.e: Europa Clipper will fly past the icy moon many times to find out whether it could support life.

Titan.q: Titan is the biggest moon of which planet?
Titan.e: Titan orbits Saturn and is bigger than the planet Mercury.

Titan.q: What fills the lakes on Titan?
Titan.e: It is so cold on Titan that gases like methane turn into liquid and form lakes.

Titan.q: What did the Huygens probe do in 2005?
Titan.e: Huygens parachuted through Titan's orange haze and landed on its surface.

Pluto.q: What kind of world is Pluto?
Pluto.e: In 2006 astronomers decided Pluto is a dwarf planet because it is small and shares its orbit with other icy objects.

Pluto.q: Which NASA spacecraft flew past Pluto in 2015?
Pluto.e: New Horizons travelled for nine years to reach Pluto and sent back amazing photos.

Pluto.q: About how long is one year on Pluto?
Pluto.e: Pluto is so far from the Sun that one lap takes 248 Earth years.

Pluto.q: What shape is the big bright glacier on Pluto?
Pluto.e: The heart-shaped region is called Tombaugh Regio and is covered in nitrogen ice.
